desc: Task 1: Prove/verify the block-length reduction — any run of length L ≥ 6 splits into 3 + (L−3), both ≥ 3; splitting never increases cost since each piece picks its own optimal char; DP only needs lengths 3, 4, 5.
Task 2: Design cost computation — 26 prefix-sum count arrays give block letter counts in O(26); cost for all 26 targets computed in O(26) via running left/right count update over the alphabet.
Task 3/4: DP design with tie-breaking — numeric suffix DP plus greedy reconstruction choosing smallest (char, len) achieving suff[i] == block_cost + suff[i+len]; avoids O(n²) string comparisons.
Task 5: Impossibility — only n < 3 is impossible; guard suff[0] == inf.
Task 6: Implement the complete solution with prefix sums, suffix DP, and greedy reconstruction.
Task 7: Verify correctness — traced all three examples, audited the incremental cost update, validated reconstruction lexicographic claim, tested edge cases; no bugs found.
